info.name: Smart Sweep SWMS API
info.description:
Smart Sweep — Solid Waste Management System for the Khulna City Corporation pilot.

Django 5.2 + DRF on PostgreSQL 18. Every endpoint under `/api/`.

## Getting started

1. Start the backend: `cd server && .venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver`
2. Select the **Smart Sweep — Local** environment.
3. Run **00 · Auth → 1 · Request login code**, then **2 · Verify code**. The test scripts capture the JWT pair, the role and the collector id into collection variables, so every other request is authorised automatically.
4. Run **01 · Catalog → Catalog bundle** to see the real ids for wards, tiers and the option lists, then point the `wardId` / `tierId` variables at them.

## Conventions

- **Auth** — collection-level Bearer `{{accessToken}}`. Access tokens are short-lived; re-run **Refresh access token** when a request answers 401 with `code: "token_invalid"`.
- **Errors** — every failure has one shape: `{"detail": "…", "code": "stable_key", "fields": {"road": ["…"]}}`. `code` is a stable key the UI maps to a translated string.
- **Pagination** — list endpoints return `{count, page, pages, next, previous, results}`. Pass `?page_size=all` for a bare array (capped at 5000).
- **Ward scoping** — applied on the server from the caller's role. It cannot be widened by a query parameter.
- **Ids are text and meaningful** — `HH-KCC-0012840`, `RT-W-14-01`, `C-042` — because field staff read them off bin stickers.

Interactive schema: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/docs/`

item.name: 00 · Auth & session
item.description: Mobile-number login by SMS code or 4-digit PIN, JWT rotation, and the operator's own profile. Run the two numbered OTP requests in order — their test scripts populate every other request's token.

request.description: The four demo personas the login screen offers as shortcuts. Returns an empty list when `DJANGO_DEBUG=False` — it would otherwise be an account-enumeration endpoint.

query.description: Mobile number in any accepted local format.

request.description: Does this number have a PIN, and is it locked out? The login screen calls this first to decide whether to offer the PIN fast path or go straight to SMS.

Issues a 4-digit code. The response also carries `known`, `hasPin` and `pinLocked` so the login screen can branch without a second round trip. In DEBUG with `OTP_EXPOSE_CODE=True`, `devCode` holds the code and this request's test script captures it into `{{otpCode}}`.

Throttled under the `otp` scope.

exec: // With OTP_EXPOSE_CODE=True and DEBUG=True the server returns the code so
// the demo can sign in without an SMS gateway. It is absent in production.
console.warn('No devCode in the response — read the code from the SMS.');

request.description: Exchanges a valid code for `{access, refresh, user}`. An unknown number is provisioned as a Collector-role 'Field Operator', which is how field staff are onboarded without a registration screen. A successful OTP also clears any PIN lockout — OTP is the recovery path.

exec: // Store the JWT pair and the signed-in operator for every later request.

request.description:
The fast path field collectors use where mobile coverage is unreliable. Returns the same `{access, refresh, user}` body as OTP verification.

An unknown number and a wrong PIN fail identically (`wrong_pin`), so this cannot be used to enumerate accounts. After `PIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` misses the account locks for `PIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS` and answers `pin_locked`.

exec: // Store the JWT pair and the signed-in operator for every later request.

request.description: Sets the signed-in operator's PIN. Requires a live access token — a PIN is set *after* an OTP sign-in, never instead of one.
Fails with `no_pin` if none is set, `wrong_pin` if `currentPin` is wrong.
Clears the PIN; the account falls back to OTP-only sign-in.
The session user: role, ward scope, `home` landing route, `readOnly` flag, and the linked `collector` id when the operator is one.
Self-service profile edit. Role and ward scope are **not** writable here — those are set by an agency admin. Returns the full user.
Rotates the refresh token. A dead token answers 401 with `{detail, code: 'token_invalid', fields}` rather than SimpleJWT's own shape, so the frontend interceptor has one envelope to branch on.
Blacklists the refresh token. Always answers `{ok: true}` — revoking an already-dead token is not an error.

item.name: 05 · Collection round & visits
item.description: What a collector's device talks to: the day's round, QR scanning, recording collections and skips, and flushing the offline queue.

request.description:
Everything the round screen renders in one call: `stops` in walking order, the three `counts` its tabs show, and the `routes` behind them for the headings.

A **collector-role** caller is pinned to their own round whatever they pass — a round names households and phone numbers. Supervisors and admins may look in on anyone, which is how a round gets reviewed from a desk.

item.name: Resolve a scan against the round

request.description:
Answers **200 in every case** — a wrong-round or worn-label scan is something the collector acts on, not a failed request.

`{ok: true, stop}` — scan is a stop on this round.
`{ok: false, reason: 'alreadyCollected', stop}` — stops a double entry.
`{ok: false, reason: 'otherRoute', ...}` — a wrong-round mistake the collector can fix on the spot.
`{ok: false, reason: 'unknown'}` — unregistered or damaged tag; needs the office.
`{ok: false, reason: 'unreadable'}` — the camera got nothing.

request.description:
**One visit per household per day**, enforced by a unique constraint on `(household, served_on)`. Re-posting for the same day updates that row rather than inserting a second one — which is exactly what correcting a skip to a collection, and the offline queue, rely on.

The tag and route are taken from the plan, not the request, and the live map is notified.
A skip needs a `reason`: `noOne` | `noWaste` | `locked` | `access` | `refused`. Correcting it later to `collected` updates the same row.

What a device flushes when it regains connectivity.

**Answers with per-row outcomes rather than one status code** — the device has to know which rows it may drop and which to keep retrying. A single bad row never rejects the batch.
Marks a queued record as having reached the server. No body.

request.description: Includes the full `activity` trail and any attached `photos`.
**`status` is not writable here.** Each lifecycle move is its own action endpoint, so a ticket cannot change hands without a trail.
Hands the ticket over — or back to the unassigned pool with `"assigned": null`. Appends an audit entry.
Moves along the lifecycle: open → assigned → in_progress → resolved → closed. Read `nextStatus` on the ticket to know where this lands.
**The SLA budget follows the priority** — re-grading changes the clock.
Records how it was resolved and stops the SLA clock.
Restarts the clock.
Appends to the trail without changing the ticket.

`multipart/form-data`. The collector app posts several at once from the camera roll, so any number of `images` parts is accepted.

**Every file is validated before the first one is stored**, so a rejected batch leaves nothing behind.

item.description: Monthly billing runs, payments including partials, collector cash hand-ins and the reconciliation they feed. Recording a payment is the only way a bill's status changes.

query.description: Derived in SQL from the payments that exist — prefer this over `status`.

request.description:
Each row carries `received`, `outstanding` and `settlement`, computed from the payments that actually exist.

Filter on **`settlement`**, not `status`: `status` is only ever as fresh as the last `recalculate()`, while `settlement` is derived in SQL and can never disagree with the figures shown.

**Agency admin only.** Returns the same summary as a real run — how many bills, for how much — without writing anything. Answers 200.

Always dry-run first: a run is the only way bills come into existence, and there is no bulk undo.

**Agency admin only.** Issues one bill per active household for the period and writes a `BillingRun` audit row. Answers 201.

Re-running the same period does not double-charge — existing bills for the month are respected.
Honours the same query parameters as the list, so the cards always describe exactly the rows shown beneath them.

item.name: Record a payment against a bill

request.description:
**The only way a bill's status changes.** `Bill.status` is a cache that `recalculate()` derives from the payments that exist, and `Household.dues` follows from that.

Partial payments are normal — post several and the bill moves unpaid → partial → paid on its own.

Open to **collectors** as well as office roles: the collector at the door is the person the cash is handed to. `collector` defaults to the signed-in collector; leave it out at the office counter, and that difference is what makes the cash reconciliation meaningful.

Returns the restated bill.

**Fails with `use_billing_run` for everyone but a superuser.** A hand-made bill would have no `run`, so the month's totals would stop describing the month and a household could quietly be charged twice. Use `POST /api/bills/generate/`.

Kept in the collection to document the refusal.

query.description: The month the money was **taken** in, not the month its bill covers.

request.description: A July bill settled in August is money received in **August** — keeping the two apart is what makes a collection lag visible.
Equivalent to `POST /bills/{id}/pay/`; prefer that one, which returns the restated bill.

**Agency admin only.** Removes a mis-keyed payment and restates the bill from what remains — returning the restated bill.

This is the one operation that can make money on record disappear, so it deliberately does not belong to the person who keyed it in. Payments are otherwise immutable: correct one by voiding it and re-recording.

item.name: 11 · Sweep AI
item.description: The floating assistant: answers from a live ward-scoped snapshot of the database, and the snapshot itself.

request.description:
Answers an operational question from a live, **ward-scoped** snapshot of the database.

With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set it reasons over that snapshot with the Claude API; without one it falls back to rule-based answers, so the panel works either way.
The exact snapshot the assistant reasons over. Exposed so the UI can show the same numbers the assistant quotes — and so its answers are auditable.
